facts.content: Patient presents with dysuria lasting for 6 days.
Patient experiences lower abdominal/suprapubic pain midline rated at 7/10, intermittent in nature.
Patient denies fever, flank/loin/lower back pain, vaginal discharge, and difficulty voiding.
facts.source_text: Denies: Fever; flank/loin/lower back pain; vaginal discharge; difficulty voiding

facts.content: First episode with no recent triggers such as exercise, dehydration, or frequent intercourse.
facts.source_text: First episode; no recent triggers (exercise, dehydration, frequent intercourse)

facts.content: Patient has a history of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
Patient is taking Mebeverine 200 mg three times a day.
Patient lives with friends and is a support worker.
Patient consumes approximately one glass of wine per week and has never smoked.
Suspected uncomplicated cystitis with dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, hematuria, afebrile by history, no flank pain, and first episode.
facts.source_text: Suspected uncomplicated cystitis — dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, hematuria; afebrile by history; no flank pain; first episode

facts.content: A 3-day course of oral antibiotics is prescribed for cystitis, with e-prescription sent to Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy, to start as soon as possible.
facts.source_text: Cystitis: 3-day oral abx prescribed; eRx to Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy; start ASAP

facts.content: Recommended hydration of 2.5–3 liters per day and consideration of cranberry juice and over-the-counter urine alkalinizing sachets as directed.
facts.source_text: Hydration: 2.5–3 L/day; consider cranberry juice; OTC urine alkalinizing sachets as directed

facts.content: Patient advised to obtain a thermometer and check temperatures.
Safety-net instructions include seeking care if worsening pain, new flank/loin pain, high fever, or difficulty passing urine occur and follow-up if not resolving after course or if recurrent.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: Seek care if worsening pain, new flank/loin pain, high fever, difficulty passing urine; f/u if not resolving after course or if recurrent

facts.content: Continue Mebeverine 200 mg three times a day for IBS.
